outcomes.text: Explain how an actor's physical and vocal skills could be used to interpret a character.
Describe a personal, creative and practical vision of how a character could be communicated to an audience through physical, vocal and spatial choices.
Explain how conventions, form and techniques create meaning.
Explain how semiotics convey meaning in the two studied performance texts.
Explain how performance space and relationships between characters on stage communicate to an audience.
Explain the relationship between actors and audience.
Explain how creative and artistic choices shape the way meaning is communicated.
Describe the collaborative processes needed to create a theatre performance.
Explain how set, lighting, sound, props, costume and make-up could be used in performance.
Show how the themes of a text (conflict, family dynamics, or heroes and villains) can be communicated in performance.
Show practical understanding of how the contexts in which the texts were written influence performance.
Show how dramatic techniques support an interpretation of a text for performance.
Justify performance decisions with evidence from practical exploration and development of character.
Articulate a personal response using accurate subject-specific terminology.
Use the meaning of drama and theatre terminology used by theatre makers.
Analyse a live theatre performance they have seen.
Evaluate the work of others, drawing considered conclusions.
Analyse and evaluate the acting, design, directing and characteristics of the performance text seen.
Explain the production process and the role of a director.
Explain directorial methods and techniques for establishing a vision and making creative and artistic choices.
Explain the impact a vision has when staging the performance text.
Explain the text's narrative and characters from practical exploration.
Analyse how the text is built: structure, language and character construction.
Explain the playwright's intentions and original performance context.
Explain the social, cultural and historical context of the text.
Show how directorial methods support interpretations and creative possibilities for staging the text.
Make directorial decisions for staging the text.
Give an informed, creative and personal interpretation of how the text can be communicated to an audience, using accurate subject-specific terminology.
